_doc: Living city (LocationManager + WorldSimulationManager). DISTRICT -> LOCATION -> PEOPLE -> FUNCTION -> EVENTS. Few locations, each with a job: who is there (cast haunts, patients' routines, staff breaks, suppliers), what you can do (services), what happens (ambient events). Times are minutes on the 06:00..30:00 dial (after midnight = +1440). 'map' is the marker position on the city map (fractions of the 320x180 art). 'discover': conditions that reveal the place on their own (start, level, rep, flag, any_flag, dim, bm); 'hidden' places are only revealed by people (patients, staff, fixers, rumours, story). 'access' gates entry (restricted). Activity per period: 0 dead, 1 quiet, 2 normal, 3 busy. Event outcomes use the incident vocabulary (EventManager.apply_outcomes) plus 'effects' (StoryManager.apply_effects) and 'patient' (a walk-in sent to your clinic).

travel._doc: Trip time = base + per_unit x map distance (fractions). Walking is free but slow and risky after dark in dangerous districts; the metro is cheap and runs 06:00-01:00 (not during a blackout, never into the Exclusion Zone); a cab is fast, costs more at night and won't go into the Zone. Same-district hops are always a short walk.

encounters.text: Three kids with a shock baton in an underpass. They want your wallet.

outcomes.text: They take sixty and run. Your hands shake for a block.

success.text: One of them recognises you. 'Leave the doc.' They melt back into the dark.

fail.text: They don't care who you are. Ninety gone and a bruise for free.

success.text: You lose them in the pipe maze.

fail.text: You trip on a grate. They take forty and a piece of your knee.

encounters.text: Transit police are scanning IDs at the gates. You have a bag full of medical tools.

outcomes.text: They log your name and wave you through. Logged is not nothing.
Fifty disappears into a glove. 'Have a safe night, doctor.'

encounters.text: Someone is slumped against a stairwell, chrome sparking at the shoulder. People step around them.

patient.line: You patched me on the stairs. I came to pay you back properly.

outcomes.text: You clamp the line and tape the joint. They'll come by the clinic.

patient.line: Stairwell... you told me to come here...

outcomes.text: You give them the address. Someone helps them up.
Not your shift.

encounters.text: A kid in a reflective jacket falls into step beside you. 'Going your way, doc? Carry this, fifty when it lands.'

success.text: Someone takes the box at the other end without a word. Fifty in your pocket.

fail.text: The box starts beeping. You drop it in a canal. Somebody saw.

outcomes.text: The kid shrugs and peels off.

encounters.text: A preacher with a cracked optic is shouting about 'the chrome that eats the soul'. A crowd listens.

locations.name: Your Clinic
locations.description: Whatever else changes, this is the one room in the city that's yours. Close the door and it's quiet. Leave it and things can walk out.

locations.name: Pipeworks Tenements
locations.description: Sixty storeys of stacked shipping units bolted to a dead aqueduct. Laundry, cook smoke, a hundred radios. Half your patients sleep here.
locations.architecture: Container stacks, rope bridges, hand-painted unit numbers.
locations.atmosphere: Damp, loud, crowded, never quite dark.

locations.name: The Rusty Valve
locations.description: A bar built into a decommissioned pump room. The Saints drink at the back, everyone else drinks carefully. If something is happening in the Sump, someone at the Valve knows.
locations.architecture: Riveted tanks for booths, a bar made from a valve wheel.

locations.name: The Flood Tunnels
locations.description: Storm drains under the Sump, dry nine months a year. Stalls on pallets, lamps on wires, and the Undermarket proper behind a curtain of chain. The people who sell you chrome by courier sell it here in person.
locations.architecture: Concrete culverts, chain curtains, a stairway that floods.

locations.name: Furnace Line Works
locations.description: Smelters, presses and a salvage yard that runs three shifts. Arms get caught in machines here every week. The yard sells what the machines spit out: scrap, parts, sometimes chrome still warm.
locations.architecture: Gantries, slag heaps, a canteen in a shipping container.
locations.atmosphere: Orange glare, shift sirens, metal on metal.

locations.name: Glow Strip Night Market
locations.description: Two kilometres of stalls under a canopy of dead advertising screens. Supplies, tools, food, fakes, and people who know people. It wakes up when the sun goes down.
locations.architecture: Stalls under screens, rickshaw lanes, noodle steam.

locations.name: The Orchid Room
locations.description: A members' lounge three floors above the Velvet Tier clubs. Fixers take meetings in the booths; performers come up between sets; someone from Meridian is always slumming. The drinks cost what a stitch costs downstairs.
locations.architecture: Black glass, orchids under UV, a booth for every secret.
locations.atmosphere: Low music, soft voices, everyone watching the door.

locations.name: Caldera Stacks
locations.description: Pre-collapse apartment blocks with working lifts and nosy neighbours. Retired surgeons, old soldiers, families who pay their bills. The old city remembers everyone.
locations.architecture: Concrete balconies, rooftop gardens, faded murals.

locations.name: Spindle Interchange
locations.description: Five metro lines and the freight lift meet under a rusted glass dome. Everyone in Caldera passes through here sooner or later: commuters, couriers, people who don't want to be followed.
locations.architecture: Glass dome, tiled tunnels, freight cages.
locations.atmosphere: Announcements, crowds, wind from the tunnels.

locations.name: Meridian Medical Plaza
locations.description: Clean white floors, licensed clinics, a Lyra Biocomp atrium with a fountain nobody drinks from. Everything is monitored. They pay well for discreet, licensed work, and some of them pay better for the other kind.
locations.architecture: White stone, glass bridges, drone lanes.

locations.name: Exclusion Checkpoint 9
locations.description: Concrete, floodlights and a turnstile. Beyond it, the Lyra Exclusion Zone: closed labs, the old research annex, things the company says never happened.
locations.architecture: Barriers, scanner arches, a guard hut with a heater.

locations.name: Lyra Research Annex
locations.description: The annex where the neural line was built. Half the floors are sealed; the other half are full of cold storage, discarded prototypes and logs nobody wiped. Every visit is borrowed time.
locations.architecture: Clean rooms gone grey, sealed doors, emergency lighting.
locations.atmosphere: Hum of freezers, your own footsteps.

routines._doc: Where people are by period: home / work / social / transit. Archetypes not listed use 'default'. 'night_shift' archetypes work at night.

haunts._doc: Where the cast can be found outside their scenes: [{loc, periods, chance}]. Presence is rolled once per day and period, so it doesn't flicker. 'unless' flags remove them.

events.title: SHOUTING ON THE BRIDGE
events.text: Two neighbours are screaming at each other across a rope bridge about a stolen battery. One has a bandaged arm that's bleeding through.

outcomes.text: You rewrap it on the spot. The shouting stops. Both of them know your name now.
The battery goes over the edge. Problem solved, sort of.

events.title: RAID
events.text: Corporate security is going unit to unit looking for 'unlicensed implant recipients'. Doors are being kicked.

outcomes.text: Doors close before the boots get there. Someone saw you running ahead of the raid.
You watch them drag a man out by his chrome arm. He looks at you.

events.title: A KID WITH A TOY ARM
events.text: A kid is showing off a plastic 'cyber arm' with blinking lights to a crowd of smaller kids. 'When I grow up the doc's gonna give me a real one.'

events.title: STACK BLACKOUT
events.text: A whole stack goes dark. Somebody's dialysis rig is on a battery with twenty minutes left.

choices.label: RIG POWER FROM YOUR KIT (2 parts)

outcomes.text: You jury-rig the rig. The family won't stop thanking you.

choices.label: TELL THEM TO COME TO THE CLINIC

patient.line: The power went... you said come...

outcomes.text: They carry him down sixty storeys. He'll be at your door.

events.title: POLICE IN THE STAIRWELL
events.text: Two officers are asking residents about 'a doctor who works under the Sump'. A neighbour is pointing at your photo.

fail.text: 'Doctor? A word.' It takes an hour and a lot of patience.

outcomes.text: Four flights up, two roofs over. Nobody follows.

events.title: POSTERS
events.text: Hand-printed posters on every lift door: MISSING. Have you seen this person? The face is someone with fresh chrome.

events.title: A NEIGHBOUR'S FAVOUR
events.text: An old woman on a balcony waves you up. Her husband's hand implant has been twitching for a week and she doesn't trust the plaza clinic.

outcomes.text: A loose connector. Forty credits and a jar of plum preserve.

patient.line: My wife says you're the good kind of doctor.

outcomes.text: He'll come by tomorrow, she says. Today, probably.

events.title: BOTTLES
events.text: A merc and a Saints runner go over a table. Glass, blood, and a chrome fist through the jukebox.

choices.label: STITCH THE LOSER AT THE BAR

outcomes.text: You close a scalp wound on the bar top. The bartender pours you one on the house.

success.text: Both of them back down when the doc says so. People notice.

fail.text: You catch an elbow. Your hands will be off for a bit.

outcomes.text: The Saints win. They usually do here.

events.title: A BOOTH IN THE BACK
events.text: A fixer you don't know slides into your booth. 'I hear you're careful. I have a client who needs careful.'

patient.line: My client sent me. Careful, they said.

outcomes.text: A client will come to the clinic. They pay well and they don't want questions.
The fixer gives you a name and a place.
'Your loss, doc.'

events.title: LOOKING FOR WORK
events.text: A woman with medic's calluses and a dishonourable discharge tattoo asks if you're the doc who's hiring.

outcomes.text: She'll be on your candidate list tomorrow morning.
She nods and goes back to her drink.

events.title: A TOAST
events.text: Someone at the bar raises a glass to 'the doc who put my brother's legs back on'. Half the room drinks.

events.title: STING
events.text: The chain curtain goes up too fast. Lights. 'Nobody move.' It's a sting, and they're scanning faces.

success.text: Cold water to the chest, but you're out.

fail.text: Caught at the outflow. A fine, a file, and a long look.

outcomes.text: Two hundred buys you a blind spot and a phone number.

events.title: A NEW TABLE
events.text: A table that wasn't here last week. Unmarked cases, a seller with no face you can remember.

outcomes.text: You open it at home. Something in there hums.
The seller doesn't talk. The woman at the next table does.
Smart, maybe.

events.title: DEAL GONE WRONG
events.text: Two sellers draw on each other over a crate. Somebody fires. A bystander goes down with a hole in their thigh.

patient.line: You held my leg together in the tunnels.

outcomes.text: You get the bleeding stopped. They'll need surgery: your door.
You're two culverts away before the second shot.

events.title: SHIPMENT
events.text: A shipment came in from the docks: surplus clinical stock, still in corporate shrink-wrap.

outcomes.text: Four packs at a market price you'll never see in the Plaza.
Three good parts.

events.title: SIREN ON LINE 3
events.text: The press on Line 3 stops with a scream. A worker's arm is in it to the shoulder. The company medic is 'on his way'.

patient.line: You got me out of the press. I need an arm, doc.

outcomes.text: You get the arm out and the bleeding stopped. They'll need a new arm. They'll come to you.
The company medic arrives forty minutes later.

events.title: SCRAP FROM THE SHREDDER
events.text: The salvage foreman has a crate of implants that came out of a scrapped security drone. 'Untested. Cheap.'

outcomes.text: Battered, but there's a working unit in there and a part to spare.
The foreman shrugs.

events.title: STRIKE
events.text: The night shift has walked out over the press on Line 3. Company security is lining up at the gate.

outcomes.text: The batons come out at midnight. Your table is the only one there.
Not your fight.

events.title: SCRAP SPARKS
events.text: A welder throws a shower of sparks into a puddle, and for a second the whole yard is gold.

events.title: RARE STOCK
events.text: A stall you've never seen has a single sealed implant under glass. 'Off a Lyra truck. Don't ask.'

outcomes.text: Lyra serials, filed off badly. It's real.
It's gone by the time you walk back past.

events.title: INSPECTION SWEEP
events.text: Inspectors in white coats are working the stalls with scanners. Vendors are throwing tarps over the good stuff.

choices.label: HELP A VENDOR HIDE THEIR STOCK

success.text: The tarp holds. The vendor owes you one.

fail.text: An inspector photographs you with your hand on the tarp.

outcomes.text: Two stalls get cleared. Prices will be up tomorrow.

events.title: WARM CHROME
events.text: A teenager is selling an implant out of a coat. It still has someone's blood on the connector.

outcomes.text: Cheap. You try not to think about whose it was.
The kid runs.

events.title: EMPTY STALLS
events.text: Half the medical stalls are empty. 'Trucks didn't come.' The ones that are open have tripled their prices.

events.title: SOMEONE KNOWS YOU
events.text: A stallholder leans over: 'You're the doc from the Sump. My cousin needs work done. I'll send him.'

patient.line: My cousin at the market sent me.

outcomes.text: One more for your waiting room.
'Next week then.'

events.title: AN OFFER IN A BOOTH
events.text: A woman in a silver coat slides a card across: a name, an address in the Heights, a number with four zeroes. 'House call. Tonight. No records.'

success.text: Two hours in a penthouse, one quiet procedure, six hundred and fifty credits.

fail.text: It was a setup. You get out with two hundred and the feeling of a camera on your back.

outcomes.text: The card goes back in the coat.

events.title: BETWEEN SETS
events.text: A dancer from downstairs sits at the bar rubbing a leg implant that's clearly running hot.

patient.line: From the Orchid Room. You said you'd look at my leg.

outcomes.text: 'Tomorrow, before my set?' Today, more likely.
She orders another.

events.title: A CORPORATE FACE
events.text: A Meridian manager is drunk and talking too loudly about 'the Lyra trials' and 'test populations in the Sump'.

choices.label: BUY HIM A DRINK AND LISTEN

outcomes.text: By the third drink he's naming wards and dates. You write it down in the toilet.
Corporate security walks him out ten minutes later.

events.title: LICENCE CHECK
events.text: A Medical Authority desk in the atrium is checking licences of 'visiting practitioners'.

fail.text: 'This licence lists an address in the Sump.' A note goes on your file.

outcomes.text: You take the service lift.

events.title: A QUIET STRETCHER
events.text: Security wheels a covered stretcher out of a Lyra suite into a freight lift. A hand slips out from under the sheet: chrome to the elbow, the same model you install.

success.text: Sub-level 3. A van with no plates. You get the number.

fail.text: A guard steps out of the lift. 'Lost, doctor?'

outcomes.text: Nobody else saw anything either.

events.title: EXTRACTION
events.text: A man in a cleaner's uniform grabs your arm. 'You're a doctor. They put something in me. Get me out of here.' Security is at the far end of the hall.

choices.label: WALK HIM OUT AS YOUR PATIENT

patient.line: You walked me out of the Plaza. They put something in me.

success.text: Out the front door, arm in arm. He'll be at your clinic.

fail.text: Security takes him at the doors. They take your name too.

outcomes.text: Security reaches him a minute later.

events.title: A JOB OFFER
events.text: A Lyra recruiter recognises your work. 'We need people with your hands. Salaried. Licensed. Clean.'

outcomes.text: You keep the card. It's heavy for a piece of plastic.
'The offer stands. For now.'

events.title: THE CLEAN CONTRACT
events.text: A Meridian admin offers a contract: two hundred credits a head to 'assess' Sump residents for a trial. Your name on the consent forms.

outcomes.text: Six hundred in advance. Your name on forty forms.
'Somebody else will sign it.' Somebody else will.

events.title: ARREST ON THE PLATFORM
events.text: Transit police pin a courier to the tiles. His bag splits: implants, unpackaged, your clinic's tape on two of them.

outcomes.text: Nobody stops you. Nobody needs to.

success.text: Your licence and a confident voice. They hand you the bag.

fail.text: They keep the bag and take your name.

events.title: A FAVOUR IN THE FREIGHT CAGE
events.text: A freight handler offers to move anything you need through the cages, no scans. 'Medical, right? Nobody checks medical.'

outcomes.text: Three supply packs land at your back door without a single form.
'Offer's open.'

events.title: LINE DOWN
events.text: A recorded voice apologises for 'a person on the tracks'. The crowd groans and starts walking.

events.title: PATROL
events.text: A patrol with dogs sweeps the fence line. Floodlights stop on you for a second too long.

events.title: A WAY IN
events.text: A scavenger with a Lyra badge on a lanyard says there's a gap in the fence behind the old water tower. 'For a price. Or for a favour, doc.'

outcomes.text: The scavenger draws it on your hand in marker. The annex is at the end of it.
A fair trade. A drawing on a scrap of foil: the gap, the annex, the guard rota.
'I'll be around.'

events.title: FOOTSTEPS
events.text: A guard is walking the corridor towards the cold room where you're standing.

success.text: Two minutes at minus twenty. He walks past.

fail.text: The door alarm. You run. They'll have your face.
He asks for your badge. You don't have one.

events.title: BED 14
events.text: In a sealed ward, one bed is still occupied: a trial subject, alive, wired into a rack that's running on battery. Their file has a Sump address.

choices.label: UNHOOK THEM AND GET THEM OUT

patient.line: Bed fourteen... you took me out...

outcomes.text: You carry them out through the gap in the fence. They need surgery tonight.
Forty pages of dosing logs. Proof, if anyone will look at it.

missing._doc: A patient who leaves your table with risky chrome can disappear (BAR -> FIXER -> BM SUPPLIER -> EXPERIMENTAL CYBERWARE -> PATIENT -> COMPLICATION -> PATIENT DISAPPEARS -> RESIDENTIAL -> INDUSTRIAL -> STORY EVENT). A relative asks for help; their home has a clue; the clue leads to where they are; what you do there decides.
clues: {relative} says they stopped sleeping after the operation. They kept saying the arm 'talked'. Last anyone saw, they were heading to {place}.
Their unit is open. The bed is soaked in coolant. A note on the wall in shaky letters: '{place} - they can take it out'.
The neighbour heard them screaming at night, then nothing. A transit receipt on the floor: {place}.
missing.found: You find {name} at {place}, curled in a corner, chrome arm locked in spasm and skin around the port gone grey. They don't recognise you at first.
